general_information.Description: This course helps students to identify the power of transmedia storytelling in attracting and influencing audiences. The students will practice designing, sharing, and participating in a cohesive story experience across multiple traditional and digital delivery platforms - for entertainment, advertising and marketing, or social change. In the end, this course will help you to design a strategy for developing and telling your own transmedia story. Lecturer will use several teaching methods such as conducting group discussion and sharing field work experiences in the market on top of regular teaching. Students will have the chance to showcase their presentation and media products as well as their thinking process related to this field. Teaching methods: '- Direct Instruction - Inquiry-based Learning - Cooperative Learning - Case Study Analysis
general_information.StudentTasks: - Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination. - Student is responsible to do all exercises, assignments and labs given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time - Use laptop in class only for learning purpose - Promptly access to the FU FLM at https://flm.fpt.edu.vn for up-to-date course information

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Shape your ideas into compelling and well structured narratives and complex story worlds
Identify, understand, and engage different audiences in your stories
Create cohesive user experiences across different platforms
Evaluate existing and emerging technologies to share your story with the world, and help your audience participate in the larger storyworld you create
Identify how to act ethically and professionally, and be accountable when professionally applying transmedia communication in real life

assessments.Grading Guide: Option 1: Students will be required to examine a story that plays a vital role in 01 media product and analyze the story through the lens of theories discussed in class. This practice is intended to help students identify basic concepts and principles of transmedia storytelling by analysing the story through such issues as: its relationship to the story world, its strategies for expanding the narrative, its deployment of the distinctive properties of its platform, its targeted audience, and some specific recent trends. Where possible, students should link their analysis to the course materials, including readings, lecture notes, and screenings. Option 2: (For Constructivism Approach only): Follow lecturer's proposal

assessments.Grading Guide: Option 1: Students with a group of 4 to 6 will conceptualize and design a transmedia narrative or experience that communicates stories across some distinct media. Sections will include: a brief description of the proposal; intended audience and evidence of its related interests; plans for communicating unique stories across distinct media platforms; a preliminary timeline for producing and promoting each of these pieces and interacting with audiences. Your project should include additional material such as storyboards, concept art, or audience research. Option 2: (For Constructivism Approach only): Follow lecturer's proposal
